semantic_findings.finding: Stored NpcSide is preserved in raw rows but LoadNpcs selects Dir=2; raw CSV is not proof that the runtime honors direction.
One equipment row exists; no reference to this table was found in the fixed Server source. File presence is not actual composite rendering.
RepairAbility exposes a stub dialogue; it does not repair durability or charge a repair price.
Each loot line rolls integer1..100000 against rate*1000 independently. Duplicate item lines are separate rolls. Non-gold amount is uniform1..maximum; gold uses the fixed stored amount.
All rare rows roll independently, then only the first successful source-order item drops. No-success is possible. Rates are not exclusive weights and must not be normalized.
HandleMobDrops requires a PC killer and also calls map-fragment and dragon-essence global handlers; literal per-monster tables alone are not the complete conditional drop system.
P1998 rolls amount1..maximum before its gold branch, unlike RTK fixed gold. Same lineage does not mean identical behavior.
Archive corrections include deliberately calibrated accessory drop rates; archive item presence does not establish those probabilities. Do not promote them as original KR rates.
Recipes has24 columns but zero INSERT rows. Crafting Lua16 files are separately indexed; an empty SQL recipe table does not prove no crafting exists.
Recipe C loader expects RecSuccessRate/RecCraftTime/materials/critical fields; no recipe probabilities can be selected from the empty dump.
NA Lua dialogues override C# abilities where present.26 indexed click/speech callbacks are not380 complete NPC dialogue graphs or KR original words.
Explicit NpcAbilities compositions can narrow an ability by NPC ID/map; otherwise shop/repair/bank flags form fallback abilities. Repair fallback still targets the stub.
Path99 is a source-defined no-normal-class marker, not a missing fifth player class; GM/proc/dog-specific acquisition paths remain separate.
C loader reads NPC look/palette/face/hair/skin/sex/direction and is-char independently. NA IDs are not identified with KR asset IDs.

The upstream reference dump contains external character authentication-related hashes, internal IPs and game-state rows. Values are never emitted; all such tables are excluded from normalized outputs. This is not evidence of the user's credentials leaking.

limitations: P1998 and RTK are linked source families, never two independent KR sources
CSV parsing confirms stored values, not that runtime loads/uses every row
Lua indexes explicitly retain partial semantic decode, not a complete dialogue/craft/skill interpreter
RTK original SQL is never executed and authentication/save tables are never emitted
All timings and probability interpretations are source-local NA references, not KR original values
